title: Flood Fury Across India: Odisha Battles Deluge, J&K Cut Off by Landslides, Assam Rolls Out Massive Relief - Open Magazine
article_text:
India's monsoon continues to leave a trail of destruction across multiple states.
In Odisha, floodwaters have affected more than 8.6 lakh people across 22 districts, forcing the evacuation of over 2.67 lakh residents. In Jammu & Kashmir, weeks of relentless rain have triggered landslides that have cut off villages, damaged schools and left entire communities struggling to stay connected. In Assam, where floodwaters are slowly receding, the government has begun distributing financial relief while preparing for long-term rehabilitation.
Together, the three states offer a snapshot of the scale of this year's monsoon challenge: rescue operations in one region, infrastructure collapse in another, and the difficult task of rebuilding in a third.
Odisha remains the worst-affected state in the latest spell of flooding.
According to the state government, floods have impacted 22 of Odisha's 30 districts, affecting 85 blocks, 656 gram panchayats and 1,458 villages. More than 8.63 lakh people have been affected, while 2.67 lakh residents have been evacuated to safer locations. Although water levels have started receding in several areas, authorities have directed district administrations to keep people in relief camps until villages become fully habitable again.

The government has announced an initial relief package of ₹110 crore, with ₹26 crore already released. Rescue teams from the NDRF, ODRAF and Fire Services continue to provide food, drinking water and other essentials across affected districts. Health authorities are also prioritising the evacuation of pregnant women and monitoring a rise in snakebite cases, a recurring threat during flood emergencies.
While Odisha battles overflowing rivers, the crisis in Jammu & Kashmir is being driven by landslides.
In Rajouri district, continuous rainfall over the past three weeks has devastated road networks, particularly around Gambir Mughlan and neighbouring panchayats in Manjakote tehsil. The key road connecting Manjakote with Thanamandi remains repeatedly blocked despite restoration efforts, leaving residents isolated.
The damage extends beyond transport. Water supply infrastructure has suffered, homes have been damaged and dozens of schools have reopened without students, as parents fear sending children across unsafe roads and collapsing bridges. Teachers continue reporting for duty despite dangerous commuting conditions, while residents are urging authorities to restore connectivity before further rainfall worsens the situation.
Assam has entered the next phase of disaster response.
Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has launched the disbursement of ₹15,000 in interim financial assistance to flood-affected families across Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Golaghat through Direct Benefit Transfer. Around 75,000 families are expected to receive assistance, with payments already reaching 62,696 households in the first phase.
The relief package goes beyond immediate cash support.
The state has announced a six-month moratorium on loan repayments for affected residents, simplified insurance claim procedures, grants for repairing damaged schools, free uniforms and textbooks for students, financial assistance for damaged Namghars, electricity bill waivers and compensation for families who lost loved ones in the floods. Officials have also been instructed to fast-track damage assessments so compensation for permanent losses can be released within weeks instead of months.
The stories unfolding in Odisha, Jammu & Kashmir and Assam illustrate the different faces of India's monsoon challenge.
In one state, authorities are still racing to rescue and shelter thousands. In another, landslides have paralysed daily life long after the rain began. Elsewhere, governments have begun the difficult transition from emergency relief to rebuilding homes, schools and livelihoods.
As the monsoon continues, officials remain on alert, warning that recovery will depend not only on receding waters but also on restoring roads, public services and normal life for millions living in flood-hit regions.

title: Delhi Rain Alert on Tuesday: Delhi is Likely to Experience Light to Moderate Rainfall Today - NativePlanet
article_text:
Light rainfall was recorded in several parts of Delhi early on Tuesday morning, bringing relief from the recent heat and humidity. The showers lowered the temperature and made the weather more pleasant for residents across the national capital.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Delhi is expected to witness generally cloudy skies throughout the day. The weather department has forecast one or two spells of light to moderate rainfall in some areas from early morning until noon. Another round of light rain is likely in many places during the evening.
The IMD has predicted that the maximum temperature will remain between 31 and 33 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is expected to be between 23 and 25 degrees Celsius.
Earlier in the day, the IMD had issued a yellow alert for Delhi until 8 am, warning of moderate rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning, and winds blowing at speeds of 30 to 40 kmph.
Meanwhile, the southwest monsoon continues to affect many parts of the country. The IMD has forecast extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places in Assam, Meghalaya, West Bengal, and Sikkim. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is also expected in Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura.
Heavy rainfall has also been predicted in Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Maharashtra, Kerala, coastal Karnataka, south Karnataka, and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
The weather department has also warned of thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of up to 50 kmph across parts of northeast, east, central and southern India. Strong winds are also expected over nearby sea areas.
The continuing spell of heavy rain has disrupted normal life in several states. Floods, landslides and waterlogging have affected many areas, especially in the northeast and southern India. Assam remains one of the worst-affected states, while several districts in Kerala have closed schools and colleges as a precaution due to forecasts of more heavy rain.
The IMD has advised people in affected areas to stay alert for waterlogging, flash floods, landslides and traffic disruptions. Fishermen have also been asked not to venture into parts of the Arabian Sea, the Lakshadweep region, the Comorin area, the Andaman Sea and adjoining parts of the south Bay of Bengal due to rough sea conditions and strong winds reaching 40-55 kmph, with gusts of up to 60-65 kmph.

title: Monsoon Floods Impact Agriculture and Infrastructure in India - Whalesbook
article_text:
Heavy monsoon rains are causing severe flooding in Assam and landslides in Kerala, impacting over 1.28 lakh people and raising concerns for standing crops. Investors should monitor potential supply chain disruptions and agricultural damage in these regions as the India Meteorological Department maintains high-alert warnings across multiple states.

As of August 4, 2026, the southwest monsoon has intensified significantly across India, leading to widespread infrastructure and agricultural disruptions. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued critical weather alerts, with Red and Orange warnings active for several states, including Assam, Kerala, Meghalaya, West Bengal, and Sikkim. These weather patterns are creating operational challenges for businesses reliant on regional logistics and agricultural output.

Impact on Regional Economy and Agriculture

Assam is facing a critical situation, with the state disaster management authority confirming 87 fatalities. With approximately 1.28 lakh people affected across seven districts, the flooding has submerged significant agricultural land. For investors tracking the consumer staples and agri-input sectors, the primary concern lies in the damage to standing crops and the potential for supply chain bottlenecks in the Northeast. Historically, such weather events in high-rainfall regions can lead to short-term inflationary pressure on local commodity prices and increased costs for companies involved in the processing and distribution of tea and other regional agricultural products.

In Kerala, ongoing landslides in hilly areas have disrupted transport networks. While the state administration is managing rescue operations, the resulting connectivity issues can hamper the movement of goods, particularly for industries dependent on timely raw material supply or last-mile delivery in the southern peninsula.

Sectoral Exposure and Operational Risks

Beyond the immediate humanitarian impact, the intensity of this year's monsoon poses operational risks. The IMD’s forecast of extremely heavy downpours exceeding 204.5 mm in isolated locations suggests that logistics and manufacturing facilities in affected zones may face temporary slowdowns. Companies with significant footprint in areas under Red and Orange alerts may experience higher operating costs due to necessary diversions or protective measures for their workforce and inventory.

While urban centers like Delhi have received moderate rainfall, the overall national pattern—marked by temperature anomalies and localized extreme weather—requires businesses to maintain robust contingency plans. The IMD has provided specific advisories for farmers, emphasizing the need for proper field drainage and crop protection to mitigate post-rain disease outbreaks, which often impact yield quality.

What Investors Should Monitor

Investors may track the pace of recovery in the affected regions over the coming weeks to gauge the extent of damage to regional harvests and infrastructure. Key monitorables include official damage assessment reports from state authorities, any notable volatility in regional agricultural commodity prices, and management commentary from companies with high geographical concentration in Assam, Kerala, and the Eastern states. The persistence of these weather conditions will be the primary factor determining whether these disruptions remain localized or carry broader implications for sectoral output and inflation.

article_text:
मध्य प्रदेश में एक बार फिर मौसम का मिजाज बदलने वाला है. प्रदेश के कई हिस्सों में बारिश की कमी के बीच राहत भरी खबर सामने आई है. मौसम वैज्ञानिकों के अनुसार, 6 अगस्त से पश्चिमी विक्षोभ (वेस्टर्न डिस्टरबेंस) एक्टिव होने जा रहा है, जिसका असर प्रदेश के कई जिलों में देखने को मिलेगा. इसके चलते भारी बारिश का नया दौर शुरू हो सकता है. फिलहाल मध्य प्रदेश में मानसून सीजन के दौरान सामान्य से 16 प्रतिशत कम बारिश दर्ज की गई है, जिससे कई क्षेत्रों में जलसंकट और खेती को लेकर चिंता बनी हुई है.

6 अगस्त से सक्रिय होगा पश्चिमी विक्षोभ

मौसम विभाग के अनुसार 6 अगस्त से प्रदेश में एक नया मौसम तंत्र प्रभावी होगा. पश्चिमी विक्षोभ के सक्रिय होने से वातावरण में नमी बढ़ेगी और कई जिलों में अच्छी बारिश होने की संभावना है. इसके प्रभाव से कुछ स्थानों पर भारी बारिश भी दर्ज की जा सकती है. मौसम विशेषज्ञों का मानना है कि यह सिस्टम प्रदेश में बारिश की कमी को कुछ हद तक पूरा करने में मददगार साबित हो सकता है.

इस सीजन में अब तक 16 प्रतिशत कम बारिश

मध्यप्रदेश में मानसून सीजन के दौरान अब तक सामान्य से 16 प्रतिशत कम बारिश हुई है. प्रदेश में औसतन 15.9 इंच बारिश दर्ज की गई है, जबकि सामान्य आंकड़ों की तुलना में करीब 3.1 इंच पानी की कमी बनी हुई है. जुलाई के अंतिम दिनों में बारिश की गतिविधियां कमजोर रहने से यह अंतर और बढ़ गया.

पूर्वी मध्यप्रदेश में सबसे ज्यादा बारिश की कमी

प्रदेश का पूर्वी हिस्सा इस समय सबसे ज्यादा बारिश की कमी झेल रहा है. जबलपुर, शहडोल, रीवा और सागर संभाग में सामान्य से करीब 20 प्रतिशत कम बारिश दर्ज की गई है. कई जिलों में स्थिति और भी गंभीर बनी हुई है.

अनूपपुर, बालाघाट, छतरपुर, छिंदवाड़ा, दमोह, डिंडोरी, जबलपुर, कटनी, मैहर, मंडला, मऊगंज, नरसिंहपुर, निवाड़ी, पांढुर्णा, पन्ना, रीवा, सागर, सतना, सिवनी, शहडोल, सीधी, सिंगरौली, टीकमगढ़ और उमरिया जिलों में सामान्य से 1 प्रतिशत से लेकर 42 प्रतिशत तक कम बारिश रिकॉर्ड की गई है.

पश्चिमी हिस्से में भी औसत से कम बरसे बादल

पश्चिमी मध्यप्रदेश में भी बारिश का प्रदर्शन सामान्य से कमजोर रहा है. भोपाल, इंदौर, उज्जैन, नर्मदापुरम और ग्वालियर-चंबल संभाग में औसतन 11 प्रतिशत कम बारिश दर्ज की गई है.

आगर-मालवा, अलीराजपुर, अशोकनगर, बैतूल, भोपाल, दतिया, धार, गुना, ग्वालियर, हरदा, झाबुआ, मुरैना, मंदसौर, नर्मदापुरम, नीमच, रायसेन, राजगढ़, रतलाम, शाजापुर, श्योपुर, शिवपुरी, उज्जैन और विदिशा जिलों में भी सामान्य से कम बारिश हुई है.

किसानों और जलाशयों को बारिश का इंतजार

बारिश की कमी का असर खेती और जल भंडारण दोनों पर दिखाई दे रहा है. कई जिलों में किसान अच्छी बारिश का इंतजार कर रहे हैं, ताकि फसलों की बढ़वार बेहतर हो सके. वहीं जलाशयों और बांधों में भी पर्याप्त पानी नहीं पहुंच पाया है. ऐसे में 6 अगस्त से शुरू होने वाला संभावित बारिश का दौर प्रदेश के लिए काफी महत्वपूर्ण माना जा रहा है.

अगले कुछ दिन रहेंगे अहम

मौसम विभाग की नजर आगामी सिस्टम पर बनी हुई है. यदि पश्चिमी विक्षोभ उम्मीद के मुताबिक सक्रिय रहा तो प्रदेश के कई जिलों में अच्छी बारिश दर्ज हो सकती है. इससे न सिर्फ बारिश की कमी कम होगी, बल्कि खेती और पेयजल व्यवस्था को भी राहत मिलने की संभावना है. फिलहाल मौसम विशेषज्ञ लोगों को मौसम विभाग के अपडेट पर नजर बनाए रखने की सलाह दे रहे हैं.

Meanwhile, Himachal Pradesh continues to face monsoon disruptions, with 109 roads blocked and several power and water supply systems affected.

NEW DELHI — The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued district-wise nowcast warnings for several states on Tuesday, cautioning residents about thunderstorms, lightning, heavy rainfall and gusty winds over the next two to three hours.

A Red warning, indicating severe weather conditions requiring immediate action, has been issued for Patiala district in Punjab. The IMD has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning, gusty winds reaching around 60 kmph, and heavy rainfall exceeding 15 mm per hour, urging residents to remain indoors and avoid unnecessary travel.

Time & Calendars

An Orange Warning has been issued for several districts across multiple states, where thunderstorms, lightning, winds of 40–60 kmph, and moderate to heavy rainfall (5–15 mm per hour or more) are very likely.

In Punjab, the warning covers Fatehgarh Sahib, Ludhiana, Sangrur and SAS Nagar. In Uttar Pradesh, the affected districts include Amethi, Ayodhya, Barabanki, Fatehpur, Hardoi, Kanpur Dehat, Kanpur Nagar, Lucknow, Pratapgarh, Raebareli and Unnao.

The alert also extends to Kasaragod in Kerala; Dakshin Kannada, Shivamogga and Udupi in Karnataka; Bhind, Datia, Gwalior, Morena, Sheopur Kalan and Shivpuri in Madhya Pradesh; Jiribam, Kamjong, Noney, Senapati and Tamenglong in Manipur; Uttar Dinajpur in West Bengal; Longleng, Mokokchung, Mon and Wokha in Nagaland; Golaghat, Jorhat, Majuli and Sivasagar in Assam; Ambala, Faridabad, Gurugram, Kaithal and Kurukshetra in Haryana; and Bageshwar, Dehradun, Pithoragarh, Tehri Garhwal and Uttarkashi in Uttarakhand.

The IMD has advised residents in all affected districts to remain vigilant and follow safety precautions. People have been urged to avoid taking shelter under trees or weak structures during thunderstorms, monitor road and traffic conditions before travelling, stay away from flood- and landslide-prone areas, and strictly follow advisories issued by local authorities and disaster management agencies.

અમદાવાદ-નવી દિલ્હીઃ હવામાન વિભાગ અનુસાર વેસ્ટર્ન ડિસ્ટર્બન્સના કારણે ઉત્તર પશ્ચિમ ભારતમાં 13 તારીખ સુધી વરસાદનો પ્રભાવ જોવા મળશે. ગાજવીજ સાથે ભારે પવન અને કરા પણ પડશે. ઉત્તર પૂર્વના રાજ્યો તથા પશ્ચિમ બંગાળમાં આગામી પાંચથી સાત દિવસ એક બે સ્થળોએ 7 થી લઈ 20 સેમી સુધી વરસાદ પડી શકે છે. દક્ષિણ ભારતના કેરળ, કર્ણાટક, તમિલનાડુમાં ભારે વરસાદનું પૂર્વાનુમાન છે. ગુજરાતમાં ચોમાસાના આગમન પહેલા મોટા ભાગના વિસ્તારમાં વાદળછાયું વાતાવરણ જોવા મળી રહ્યું છે. દક્ષિણ ગુજરાતમાં છૂટાછવાયા સ્થળોએ  હળવા વરસાદી ઝાપટાં પડી રહ્યા છે.

 

ગુજરાતમાં કેવું રહેશે હવામાન

 

આજે સુરત સહિત દક્ષિણ ગુજરાતમાં પવન સાથે વરસાદની શક્યતા વ્યક્ત કરવામાં આવી છે. 16 જૂન સુધી દક્ષિણ ગુજરાત, સૌરાષ્ટ્ર અને મધ્ય ગુજરાતમાં છૂટાછવાયા સ્થળોએ હળવાથી મધ્યમ વરસાદની શક્યતા છે. નૈઋત્યનું ચોમાસું ગુજરાત તરફ ધીમે ધીમે આગળ વધી રહ્યું છે, જેના પગલે સક્રિય થયેલી વરસાદી સિસ્ટમ રાજ્યના વિવિધ ભાગોમાં જોવા મળી શકે છે. 12 થી 16 જૂન દરમિયાન દક્ષિણ ગુજરાત, મધ્ય ગુજરાત અને સૌરાષ્ટ્રમાં છૂટાછવાયા સ્થળોએ હળવોથી મધ્યમ વરસાદ વરસી શકે છે. અમદાવાદમાં આજે મહત્તમ તાપમાન 42 ડિગ્રી આસપાસ રહી શકે છે. લોકોને કાળઝાળ ગરમી અને બફારાનો અનુભવ થશે.

 

ચોમાસું ક્યાં પહોંચ્યું?

 

ચોમાસું આગામી ત્રણથી ચાર દિવસમાં મહારાષ્ટ્ર, કર્ણાટક, તેલંગાણા, આંધ્રપ્રદેશમાં આગળ વધી શકે છે અને તમિલનાડુના બાકીના ભાગોને પણ આવરી શકે છે. આ દરમિયાન છત્તીસગઢ, બિહાર, ઝારખંડ, ઓડિશાના કેટલાક ભાગોમાં ચોમાસું દસ્તક આપી શકે છે. ચોમાસાને આગળ વધવા માટે સાનુકૂળ પરિસ્થિતિઓ છે. વેસ્ટર્ન ડિસ્ટર્બન્સના કારણે મધ્ય ભાગમાં લો પ્રેશર સર્જાયું છે. આ કારણે ઉત્તર-પશ્ચિમ ભારતમાં આગામી 24 કલાકમાં તાપમાનમાં કોઈ મોટો ફેરફાર જોવા નહીં મળે. ત્યારબાદ 13 તારીખ સુધી પારો 3 થી 5 ડિગ્રી સેલ્સિયસ સુધી ગગડી શકે છે. જે પછી તાપમાન ફરીથી 2 થી 4 ડિગ્રી સુધી વધી શકે છે. દેશના મધ્ય ભાગમાં આગામી 3 દિવસ એટલે કે 12 તારીખ સુધી તાપમાનમાં બહુ ફેરફાર જોવા નહીં મળે, પરંતુ ત્યારબાદ તાપમાનમાં 2 થી 3 ડિગ્રી સુધીનો ઘટાડો જોવા મળી શકે છે. પૂર્વ ભારતમાં 2 દિવસ સુધી તાપમાનમાં ખાસ ફેરફાર નહીં થાય. ત્યારબાદ 12 થી 14 તારીખ વચ્ચે તાપમાનમાં 2 થી 4 ડિગ્રી સુધીનો ઘટાડો થઈ શકે છે.

 

 

 

મધ્યપ્રદેશ-બિહારમાં ઓરેન્જ એલર્ટ

 

પૂર્વી મધ્યપ્રદેશ, ઝારખંડ, ઓડિશા અને બિહાર, પશ્ચિમ બંગાળ, આસામ, મેઘાલયમાં ઓરેન્જ એલર્ટ જાહેર કરવામાં આવ્યું છે. આ સાથે અંદામાન અને નિકોબાર ટાપુઓમાં પણ ઓરેન્જ એલર્ટ અપાયું છે. ગાજવીજ સાથે વીજળી અને તેજ પવનની અસર જોવા મળશે. આસામ, મેઘાલય, પશ્ચિમ બંગાળ અને સિક્કિમમાં એક કે બે સ્થળોએ ભારે વરસાદ પડી શકે છે. ભારે વરસાદની અસર અરૂણાચલ પ્રદેશ, નાગાલેન્ડ, મણિપુર, ત્રિપુરા, તેલંગાણા, કર્ણાટક, દક્ષિણ કોંકણ, દરિયાકાંઠાના કર્ણાટક, કેરળ, તમિલનાડુ અને લક્ષદ્વીપમાં જોવા મળશે. કર્ણાટક, ગોવા, કેરળમાં 30 થી 40 કિમીની ઝડપે પવન ફૂંકાઈ શકે છે.

 

યુપી-કાશ્મીરમાં હીટવેવનો પ્રકોપ યથાવત રહેશે

 

જમ્મુ-કાશ્મીર, હિમાચલ પ્રદેશ, ઉત્તર પ્રદેશ, પંજાબ, હરિયાણા, રાજસ્થાનમાં હીટવેવનો પ્રકોપ ચાલુ રહેશે. વેસ્ટર્ન ડિસ્ટર્બન્સના કારણે જમ્મુ-કાશ્મીર, પંજાબ, હરિયાણા, ઉત્તર પ્રદેશ અને ઉત્તરાખંડમાં કરા પડી શકે છે. આ તમામ સ્થળોએ ઓરેન્જ એલર્ટ જાહેર કરવામાં આવ્યું છે. રાજસ્થાન અને ઉત્તર પ્રદેશમાં એક-બે સ્થળોએ ધૂળની ડમરીઓ સાથે આંધી આવવાની સંભાવના છે. પૂર્વ ભારતમાં ભારે પવન અને ગાજવીજ સાથે વીજળીનો પ્રભાવ જોવા મળી શકે છે.

title: Monsoon Shifts East: Assam, Meghalaya Face Heavy Rain Alerts - Whalesbook
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy to extremely heavy rainfall for Assam and Meghalaya over the next 48 hours. This shift in the monsoon trough brings intense weather to the North-East while conditions improve in parts of Central and West India. Investors in sectors like agriculture, infrastructure, and logistics may monitor potential disruptions in the region.

The monsoon pattern across India has entered a new phase, with weather activity concentrating heavily over the North-East. According to the latest update from the India Meteorological Department, Assam and Meghalaya are currently under alerts for torrential rainfall that is expected to persist over the next two days. This movement marks a departure from recent weeks, where the primary focus of monsoon precipitation was over Central and West India.

Monsoon Trough Realignment

The shift is driven by the repositioning of the monsoon trough, which is a low-pressure area that directs moisture-laden winds across the country. As of Tuesday, this corridor has aligned to stretch from Anupgarh in Rajasthan through Delhi, Lucknow, Daltonganj, and Murshidabad, extending further toward Manipur. This configuration is actively channeling high levels of moisture into the eastern and northeastern parts of the country.

Expected Impact on North-East States

The weather forecast indicates that the North-East will experience widespread rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning. While Assam and Meghalaya are expected to face the most immediate intensity, the forecast suggests that the weather system will remain active across Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura for approximately six days. Arunachal Pradesh is also expected to receive significant rainfall in the near term.

Sector Context and Investor Focus

For investors and market observers, this weather shift has several implications. Prolonged, heavy rainfall in the North-East can often lead to logistics and supply chain challenges, particularly for transport and infrastructure projects in hilly terrain. Additionally, while the monsoon is essential for agriculture, extreme flooding can pose risks to standing crops in these regions.

Conversely, the easing of rainfall in Central and West India—areas that previously faced intense, record-breaking downpours—may provide some relief to industrial and agricultural operations that were impacted by high water levels. Monitoring the situation remains important, as the intensity and duration of these rains will determine if there is any impact on local operations, regional infrastructure projects, or supply routes. Investors typically track regional monsoon performance as it influences rural demand and inflationary trends related to food prices, though the impact of this specific weather event will depend on the duration and severity of the rainfall in the coming days.

title: IMD issues red alert for parts of Meghalaya; heavy rain may trigger floods downstream in Assam - Hub News
article_text:
East Khasi Hills, Jaintia Hills among districts expected to receive extremely heavy rainfall over next three days

Guwahati, Aug. 4: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast another spell of extremely heavy rainfall over parts of Meghalaya over the next three days, prompting authorities to warn of possible landslides, flash floods and waterlogging within the state, while also raising concerns over downstream flooding in neighbouring Assam. According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), the IMD has issued orange and red warnings for East Khasi Hills, West Jaintia Hills and East Jaintia Hills between August 3 and 5. Heavy rainfall has also been forecast for parts of Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland.

The forecast comes at a crucial time, with much of the region still recovering from successive waves of monsoon rain. Earlier this month, intense rainfall over the Meghalaya plateau and adjoining hill catchments contributed to flooding in several downstream districts of Upper Assam, inundating villages, damaging infrastructure and disrupting transport links.

Meteorologists say rainfall over the Khasi and Jaintia Hills often feeds rivers flowing into Assam, making weather conditions in Meghalaya a critical factor in flood management across the region.

Apart from the downstream impact, the IMD warning also points to the risk of localised flooding, waterlogging, slow vehicular movement and landslides in vulnerable pockets. Authorities have advised residents, especially those living in low-lying and hillside areas, to remain vigilant and avoid unnecessary travel during periods of intense rainfall.

The weather system is also expected to influence several districts of Assam. ASDMA said Cachar, Dima Hasao, West Karbi Anglong, Biswanath, Lakhimpur, Dhemaji and Tinsukia could experience the impact of rainfall originating in Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh, while showers over Nagaland may affect Charaideo, Sivasagar, Jorhat and Golaghat.

Emergency response agencies in the region have been placed on alert, and authorities have urged the public to follow official weather bulletins and advisories as the situation evolves.

title: Assam flood: Over 4.45 lakh affected in six districts - morungexpress.com
article_text:
Volunteers distribute relief materials to flood-affected residents using a tractor following heavy monsoon rains in Assam's Sivasagar district on July 27, 2026. (IANS Photo)

Guwahati, July 28 (IANS): Assam's flood situation remained critical, with over 4.45 lakh people affected across six districts, even as rescue and relief operations were intensified by the state administration, officials said on Tuesday.

According to the latest report issued by the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), floodwaters have impacted 4,45,385 people in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon and Kamrup (Metropolitan) districts.

Charaideo is the worst-affected district with nearly 1.88 lakh affected people, followed by Sivasagar where around 1.44 lakh residents have been hit by the deluge.

The ASDMA said 631 villages under 21 revenue circles remain submerged. Although the floods in Charaideo have caused widespread damage to homes, roads, educational institutions and agricultural land, no human casualties have been reported so far.

The inundation has affected 37,139.52 hectares of cropland, while more than 2.56 lakh livestock have been impacted. Officials said over 26,000 domestic animals have been washed away in the floods.

Among the major rivers, the Dhansiri (South) at Numaligarh continued to flow above the danger level, though no river has crossed its highest flood level.

The state government has stepped up relief efforts by operating 184 relief camps and distribution centres, where 28,695 displaced people are currently taking shelter. The inmates include 97 pregnant or lactating women and 42 persons with disabilities.

Rescue operations are continuing with personnel from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and district administrations deploying 67 boats to evacuate stranded residents.

Floodwaters have also damaged critical infrastructure. Authorities reported that 171 houses were completely destroyed and 4,667 others suffered partial damage.

Several roads in Sivasagar, Jorhat and Charaideo have either been breached or submerged, while several primary schools have also reported flooding and structural damage.

Urban flooding was reported from Chandmari in Guwahati under the Dispur revenue circle, though no displacement of residents was recorded.

Meanwhile, Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) Assam president Ahmad Ali Ayyubi said around 2,400 flood-affected families have received relief materials so far. He added that both Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma are monitoring the situation closely, while the state government has ensured the supply of essential ration items in the affected areas.

मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, 4 अगस्त से 8 अगस्त के बीच दिल्ली-एनसीआर में बादल छाए रहेंगे और सुबह, शाम व रात के समय बारिश (Weather Forecast) होने की संभावना है। इस दौरान 30 से 40 किमी प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से हवाएं भी चल सकती हैं। 4 अगस्त के लिए दिल्ली में येलो अलर्ट जारी किया गया है।

दिल्ली-एनसीआर और उत्तर प्रदेश में कैसा रहेगा मौसम? (Delhi NCR Ka Mausam)

मौसम विभाग के अनुसार दिल्ली, पंजाब, हरियाणा और चंडीगढ़ में 4 से 6 अगस्त के दौरान बारिश होने की संभावना है। वहीं पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश में 3 से 7 अगस्त तक और पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश में 8 अगस्त तक बारिश का दौर जारी रह सकता है। नोएडा और गाजियाबाद सहित पूरे पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश में भी इसी तरह का मौसम बने रहने के आसार हैं।




मध्य प्रदेश और छत्तीसगढ़ में बढ़ेंगी वर्षा गतिविधियां (MPCG Weathe Update)

मौसम विभाग के अनुसार 4 अगस्त से पूरे मध्य प्रदेश में वर्षा गतिविधियों में तेजी आएगी। अधिकांश जिलों में गरज-चमक के साथ हल्की से मध्यम बारिश होगी, जबकि कुछ स्थानों पर भारी बारिश और वज्रपात की संभावना है। 6 से 9 अगस्त के बीच प्रदेश में 50 किमी प्रति घंटे तक की रफ्तार से हवाएं चल सकती हैं। भोपाल, उज्जैन, इंदौर और पूर्वी मध्य प्रदेश में 5 से 9 अगस्त तक बारिश का अलर्ट है। वहीं छत्तीसगढ़ में 9 अगस्त तक और विदर्भ में 7-8 अगस्त तक बारिश की संभावना बनी हुई है।

राजस्थान और उत्तराखंड में भी भारी बारिश की आशंका

पूर्वी राजस्थान में भारी बारिश की संभावना जताई गई है। वहीं उत्तराखंड के कई इलाकों में अगले कुछ दिनों तक भारी वर्षा हो सकती है। मौसम विभाग ने कुछ स्थानों पर आंधी, तूफान और वज्रपात की भी चेतावनी जारी की है।

हिमालयी राज्यों और पूर्वोत्तर भारत में भी अलर्ट

जम्मू-कश्मीर, हिमाचल प्रदेश और उत्तराखंड में 3 से 7 अगस्त तक भारी बारिश का अनुमान है। यहां 30 से 40 किमी प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से तेज हवाएं चलने के साथ बिजली गिरने और आंधी-तूफान की आशंका भी जताई गई है।

मौसम विभाग के अनुसार अगले 7 दिनों तक अरुणाचल प्रदेश, असम, मेघालय, पश्चिम बंगाल और सिक्किम में भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश हो सकती है। इसके अलावा केरल और कर्नाटक में भी एक सप्ताह तक कई स्थानों पर तेज बारिश का अनुमान है। वहीं झारखंड में 7 अगस्त, बिहार में 5 अगस्त, पश्चिम बंगाल में 4 से 9 अगस्त और अंडमान एवं निकोबार द्वीप समूह में 4 से 9 अगस्त तक बारिश का अलर्ट जारी किया गया है।

Jharkhand Weather Update रांची: झारखंड में मंगलवार 4 अगस्त 2026 को मानसून पूरी तरह सक्रिय बना हुआ है। भारतीय मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (IMD) ने राज्य के अधिकांश हिस्सों में भारी बारिश, वज्रपात और तेज आंधी को लेकर अलर्ट जारी किया है। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार अगले पांच दिनों तक राज्य के कई जिलों में रुक रुक कर तेज बारिश का सिलसिला जारी रहने की संभावना है। लोगों को खराब मौसम के दौरान सतर्क रहने और अनावश्यक रूप से खुले स्थानों में जाने से बचने की सलाह दी गई है।

हवा में नमी का स्तर 79 प्रतिशत से 96 प्रतिशत तक रहने की संभावना है। ऐसे में बारिश के बीच उमस भी लोगों को परेशान कर सकती है।

Jharkhand Weather Update: 50 से 60 किमी प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से चल सकती है तेज हवा

आईएमडी ने चेतावनी दी है कि कई इलाकों में बारिश के दौरान 50 से 60 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से तेज हवाएं चल सकती हैं। तेज हवा के साथ वज्रपात की भी आशंका जताई गई है। मौसम विभाग ने लोगों से पेड़ों के नीचे खड़े नहीं होने, खुले मैदानों से दूर रहने और खराब मौसम के दौरान सुरक्षित स्थानों पर रहने की अपील की है।

Jharkhand Weather Update: इन जिलों में भारी बारिश और वज्रपात का अलर्ट

मौसम विभाग ने राज्य के कई जिलों में भारी बारिश और बिजली गिरने की चेतावनी जारी की है। इनमें प्रमुख रूप से पलामू, गढ़वा, लातेहार, रांची, रामगढ़, हजारीबाग, जमशेदपुर, सरायकेला, दुमका, देवघर, गोड्डा और जामताड़ा शामिल हैं। इन जिलों में स्थानीय प्रशासन को भी सतर्क रहने के निर्देश दिए गए हैं।

यदि मौसम का यही रुख बना रहा तो अगले पांच दिनों के दौरान कई क्षेत्रों में अच्छी बारिश दर्ज की जा सकती है, जिससे खेती को लाभ मिलने की संभावना है। हालांकि तेज बारिश और वज्रपात के कारण लोगों को अतिरिक्त सावधानी बरतने की जरूरत होगी।

Punjab-Haryana HC का ऐतिहासिक फैसला, देशभर में लागू होगा आर्बिट्रेशन अवार्ड

झज्जर में जलभराव से बढ़ी मुश्किलें

बारिश का सबसे अधिक और मिला-जुला असर झज्जर जिले में देखने को मिला। यहाँ मूसलाधार बारिश के चलते निचले इलाकों और प्रमुख सड़कों पर पानी भर गया। जलभराव की स्थिति पैदा होने से सुबह दफ्तर जाने वाले लोगों और वाहन चालकों को आवाजाही में काफी कठिनाइयों का सामना करना पड़ा। हालांकि, जलभराव की इस आफत के बावजूद तापमान में आई भारी गिरावट ने मौसम को सुहाना बना दिया, जिससे स्थानीय निवासियों ने चैन की सांस ली।

4 से 6 अगस्त तक अधिकांश जिलों में बारिश के प्रबल आसार

चौधरी चरण सिंह हरियाणा कृषि विश्वविद्यालय (HAU), हिसार के कृषि मौसम विज्ञान विभाग के विभागाध्यक्ष डॉ. मदन खीचड़ ने मौसम को लेकर महत्वपूर्ण जानकारी दी है। उनके अनुसार, राज्य में मानसून एक बार फिर से पूरी तरह सक्रिय हो रहा है। उत्तर-पूर्वी राजस्थान के ऊपर बने एक नए मौसमी सिस्टम (Weather System) के कारण हरियाणा में मानसूनी हवाओं की रफ्तार तेज होने की पूरी संभावना है।

इस सिस्टम के प्रभाव से 4 अगस्त से 6 अगस्त के बीच प्रदेश के ज्यादातर जिलों में गरज-चमक, तेज हवाओं और बिजली चमकने के साथ झमाझम बारिश होने के आसार हैं। इस दौरान कुछ चुनिंदा स्थानों पर भारी बारिश भी दर्ज की जा सकती है, जिससे खेतों में नमी बढ़ेगी और सूखे जैसे हालात से राहत मिलेगी।

7 और 8 अगस्त को कैसा रहेगा मौसम का मिजाज?

मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक, 4 से 6 अगस्त के बाद यानी 7 और 8 अगस्त को मौसम के मिजाज में हल्का बदलाव देखने को मिल सकता है:

आसमान की स्थिति: इन दो दिनों में राज्य के अधिकांश हिस्सों में आसमान में आंशिक रूप से बादल छाए रहने की संभावना है।

बारिश का अनुमान: कुछ छिटपुट स्थानों पर ही हल्की बूंदाबांदी या हल्की बारिश हो सकती है।

तापमान पर असर: लगातार छाए रहने वाले बादलों के कारण दिन के अधिकतम तापमान में हल्की गिरावट बनी रहेगी, जिससे गर्मी ज्यादा परेशान नहीं करेगी। हालांकि, न्यूनतम (रात का) तापमान थोड़ा बढ़ सकता है, जिससे उमस का हल्का अहसास हो सकता है।

कुल मिलाकर, आने वाले कुछ दिन हरियाणा के लोगों के लिए गर्मी से राहत भरे रहने वाले हैं, हालांकि स्थानीय निकायों को जलभराव जैसी समस्याओं से निपटने के लिए पूरी तरह सतर्क रहना होगा।

article_text:
Bihar Weather Update: बिहार के 10 जिलों में भारी और अति भारी बारिश का अलर्ट, तापमान में गिरावट से उमस से राहत
BY PRABHAT RANJAN
EDITED BY: NISHANT BHARTI
UPDATED: TUE, 04 AUG 2026 07:29 AM (IST)

बिहार में मानसून सक्रिय है, जिससे लगातार बारिश हो रही है और तापमान गिरने से उमस से राहत मिली है। मौसम विभाग ने अगले 24 घंटों में राजधानी सहित कई जिलों ...और पढ़ें

बिहार का मौसम ( एआई जेनरेटेड तस्वीर )

HIGHLIGHTS

बिहार में मानसून सक्रिय, तापमान गिरने से उमस से राहत।

10 जिलों में भारी से अति भारी बारिश का अलर्ट जारी।

अगले 48 घंटों में 2-4 डिग्री तापमान गिरेगा।

जागरण संवाददाता, पटना। प्रदेश में मानसून का प्रभाव बने होने से वर्षा की स्थिति बनी हुई है। वर्षा की गतिविधियां बने होने के साथ तापमान में गिरावट आने से लोगों को उमस से राहत मिली है। मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र पटना के अनुसार अगले 24 घंटे के दौरान राजधानी सहित सभी जिलों में बादलों की आवाजाही बने होने के साथ रिमझिम वर्षा की स्थिति बनी रहेगी। 

राज्य के 10 जिलों के अररिया, भोजपुर, बक्सर, कटिहार, किशनगंज, सारण, सिवान में भारी वर्षा एवं समस्तीपुर, वैशाली एवं पश्चिम चंपारण जिले में अति भारी वर्षा को लेकर चेतावनी जारी की गई है। 

तापमान में दो से चार डिग्री सेल्सियस की गिरावट 

48 घंटे के दौरान अधिकतम तापमान में दो से चार डिग्री सेल्सियस की गिरावट का पूर्वानुमान है। बीते 24 घंटे के दौरान प्रदेश के अलग-अलग भागों में वर्षा दर्ज की गई। 98.0 मिमी सारण के अमनौर में सर्वाधिक वर्षा दर्ज की गई। सावन की पहली सोमवारी पर इंद्रदेव की कृपा बनी रही। 

विज्ञापन हटाएं
सिर्फ खबर पढ़ें

राजधानी समेत मुजफ्फरपुर, समस्तीपुर, सुपौल आदि जगहों पर भारी वर्षा से कई स्थानों पर जलजमाव की स्थिति बनी रही। सुबह में झमाझम वर्षा के कारण मौसम सामान्य बना रहा। 25 जिलों में आंधी-पानी की स्थिति बनी रही। कई स्थानों पर हवा की 30-40 किमी प्रतिघंटा दर्ज की गई। सोमवार को पटना सहित 11 जिलों के अधिकतम तापमान में गिरावट दर्ज की गई। 

पटना का अधिकतम तापमान 30.0 डिग्री सेल्सियस

पटना का अधिकतम तापमान 30.0 डिग्री सेल्सियस एवं 35.1 डिग्री सेल्सियस के साथ सुपौल में सर्वाधिक तापमान दर्ज किया गया। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार मानसून ट्रफ बीकानेर, दिल्ली, लखनऊ, पटना होते हुए मणिपुर की ओर से होकर गुजर रही है। इसके प्रभाव से अगले तीन से चार दिनों के दौरान अलग-अलग जिलों में भारी और अति भारी वर्षा की गतिविधियां बने रहने की संभावना है।

प्रमुख स्थानों पर दर्ज हुई वर्षा 

पूर्णिया के गौरा में 92 मिमी, कस्बा में 72 मिमी, सीतामढ़ी के सोनबरसा में 60 मिमी, रोहतास के तिलौथू में 59 मिमी, सिवान के भगवानपुर हाट में 53 मिमी ,कटिहार के आजमनगर में 52 मिमी, भभुआ में 51 मिमी, सीतामढ़ी के डुमरा में 49 मिमी, मधेपुरा में 47 मिमी, सारण के मकेर में 47 मिमी दर्ज की गई।

सुपौल के बीरपुर में 45 मिमी, भभुआ के चैनपुर में 40 मिमी, बांका के अमरपुर में 40 मिमी, सहरसा के सौर बाजार में 39 मिमी, सीतामढ़ी के बेलसंड 39 मिमी, औरंगाबाद के बारूण में 36 मिमी, पुनपुन में 30 मिमी दर्ज की गई।

पूर्णिया के ढेंगराघाट में 29.4 मिमी, सिवान के रघुनाथपुर में 29 मिमी, बेगूसराय के बरौनी में 28 मिमी, रोहतास के इंद्रपुरी में 27 मिमी एवं सीतामढ़ी के परिहार में 26 मिमी वर्षा दर्ज की गई।

title: हिंद महासागर में बदला मौसम का मिजाज! अगले 2 हफ्ते एक्टिव रहेगा मॉनसून, दिल्ली-UP समेत इन राज्यों में भारी बारिश की चेतावनी - Janbhawna Times
article_text:
हिंद महासागर में बदला मौसम का मिजाज! अगले 2 हफ्ते एक्टिव रहेगा मॉनसून, दिल्ली-UP समेत इन राज्यों में भारी बारिश की चेतावनी

हिंद महासागर और बंगाल की खाड़ी में बदलती परिस्थितियों के बीच अगले दो हफ्तों तक मॉनसून सक्रिय रहने और कई हिस्सों में अच्छी बारिश होने की संभावना है.

नई दिल्ली: भारत में दक्षिण-पश्चिम मॉनसून इस समय सक्रिय दौर से गुजर रहा है. मौसम से जुड़े संकेतों के मुताबिक, अगले करीब दो सप्ताह तक देश के कई हिस्सों में बारिश की गतिविधियां बढ़ सकती हैं. उत्तर और पूर्वी भारत में छोटे-छोटे बारिश वाले सिस्टम सक्रिय हो रहे हैं. वहीं, बंगाल की खाड़ी के दक्षिणी हिस्से में भी ऐसे मौसमी बदलाव हो रहे हैं, जो बादल और बारिश को बढ़ावा दे सकते हैं.

इतिहास

दो हफ्ते तक सक्रिय रह सकता है मॉनसून

मौसम विशेषज्ञों के अनुसार उत्तर और पूर्वी भारत में कम अवधि वाले सिस्टम लगातार बन रहे हैं. इनके कारण कई क्षेत्रों में बारिश के दौर देखने को मिल सकते हैं. इसके अलावा मैडेन-जूलियन ऑसिलेशन (MJO) भी ऐसे चरण की ओर बढ़ रहा है, जो दक्षिणी बंगाल की खाड़ी में बादल बनने और बारिश के लिए अनुकूल माना जाता है.

MJO उष्णकटिबंधीय क्षेत्रों में बनने वाला एक बड़ा मौसमी पैटर्न है, जो अलग-अलग क्षेत्रों में बादल और बारिश की गतिविधियों को प्रभावित करता है. इसका अनुकूल चरण भारतीय क्षेत्र में नमी बढ़ाने में मदद कर सकता है.

हिंद महासागर में समुद्री बदलाव

हिंद महासागर में इस समय इंडियन ओशन डाइपोल (IOD) न्यूट्रल स्थिति में है. यानी समुद्र की सतह के तापमान का वह पैटर्न फिलहाल पूरी तरह विकसित नहीं हुआ है, जो मॉनसून की दिशा को काफी प्रभावित कर सके.

हालांकि, इंडोनेशिया और जावा के आसपास समुद्र की सतह का तापमान धीरे-धीरे कम हो रहा है. इसका एक कारण समुद्र की गहराई से ठंडे पानी का ऊपर आना यानी अपवेलिंग माना जा रहा है. समुद्र के तापमान में इस तरह के बदलाव आसपास के मौसम और बारिश के पैटर्न को प्रभावित कर सकते हैं.

अल-नीनो पर भी नजर

ज़्यादा जानें मनोरंजन समाचार सेवा शिक्षा समाचार अपडेट रसायन शास्त्र

मौसम वैज्ञानिक अल-नीनो की स्थिति पर भी नजर बनाए हुए हैं. यदि अल-नीनो मजबूत होता है तो इसका असर हिंद महासागर के मौसमी पैटर्न पर पड़ सकता है. हालांकि पॉजिटिव IOD विकसित होने की स्थिति में वह अल-नीनो के बारिश विरोधी प्रभाव को कुछ हद तक कम कर सकता है.

उत्तर और पूर्व भारत में बढ़ेगी बारिश

अगले दो सप्ताह के दौरान उत्तर भारत, पूर्वी भारत और बंगाल की खाड़ी से सटे इलाकों में बारिश की गतिविधियां बढ़ने की संभावना है. स्थानीय निम्न दबाव वाले सिस्टम और MJO की अनुकूल स्थिति कई क्षेत्रों में अच्छी बारिश करा सकती है.

फिलहाल IOD न्यूट्रल है, इसलिए पूरे मॉनसून सीजन का रुख तय करना जल्दबाजी होगी. समुद्र के तापमान, अल-नीनो और वायुमंडलीय बदलावों पर लगातार नजर रखी जा रही है.

title: 2 killed as cloudbursts, flash floods wreak havoc across J&K - thekashmirimages.com
article_text:
Srinagar: Two persons were killed and dozens rescued on Monday as multiple cloudbursts and flash floods triggered by heavy rain caused widespread damage across Jammu and Kashmir, disrupting road connectivity and damaging homes, bridges and agricultural land.
According to officials, a woman died after a cloudburst triggered flash floods in the Himli area of Lolab in Kupwara district. The deceased was identified as Naseema Begum, wife of Mohammad Ayub of Warnow.
In a separate incident, a man drowned in a water body in Singhpora area of Baramulla district during the inclement weather. He was identified as Murtaza Bashir, son of Bashir Ahmad Lone of Boniyar.
Shopian was the worst-hit district in Kashmir, where cloudbursts in the upper reaches triggered flash floods in Zawoora, Badrhama and Kijarsinda villages. Floodwaters entered several houses in Badrhama, damaging household belongings and inundating agricultural fields.
The State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) evacuated around 80 people, including schoolchildren and staff, from the affected areas. Officials said no casualties were reported from Shopian, although several houses and public infrastructure suffered damage.
In Anantnag district, a cloudburst at Batkoot in Pahalgam damaged a kacha house, while heavy rain caused the collapse of the rear retaining wall of the Nunwan base camp, allowing water to enter the camp and damage several accommodation tents. Officials said the situation was later brought under control.
The Aishmuqam-Pahalgam road was blocked near Langnai Bridge due to flooding, while a bridge at Batkoot also sustained damage.
Another cloudburst in the Arin-Dardpora area of Bandipora district damaged roads at several locations, disrupting movement.
In Ganderbal district, strong winds blew off the roof of a house in Bakura village and damaged an electricity pole. No injuries were reported. (KNO)
Traffic movement on the Jammu-Srinagar national highway was suspended Monday evening as heavy rains lashed wide parts of Jammu and Kashmir including the border district of Rajouri, where the administration has issued an advisory urging people inhabiting flood-prone areas to remain alert.
A stretch of the Jammu-Srinagar national highway (NH-44) in Samroli area of Udhampur district became very muddy and slippery due to incessant rainfall, prompting suspension of traffic movement on both carriageways around 5 pm, a traffic police official said.
The official said the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has rushed personnel and machinery to the affected site and restoration works are underway to make the highway motorable at the earliest.
The closure of the key highway left hundreds of vehicles stranded on both ends, officials said.
The traffic police have advised commuters to avoid travelling on NH-44 until the road is declared safe for vehicular movement.
In Rajouri, a temporary house suffered extensive damage in a mudslide triggered by heavy rainfall at Shahpur village in Kotranka area, officials said, adding that occupants of the house escaped unhurt.
Heavy rain lashed most parts of Rajouri since Monday afternoon, prompting the district administration to issue an advisory for residents living in flood-prone areas, urging them to remain alert in view of the prevailing conditions and the possibility of a sudden rise in water levels in rivers and streams.
Vulnerable areas identified by the administration include the vicinity of the CEO office, Naban Mohalla (riverbank houses), Tariq Bridge area, MLA Housing Colony, low-lying areas of Nowshera town, Bela area of Nowshera and adjoining residential localities, and other habitations situated along riverbanks and flood channels.
Additional vulnerable areas include Peeri, Koteranka, Darhal and downstream villages of Rajouri and Nowshera.
The administration has advised residents of these areas to voluntarily shift elderly persons, children, pregnant women, persons with disabilities and essential belongings to safer locations without waiting for water levels to rise.
Citizens have also been asked to remain prepared for evacuation at short notice and cooperate with police, State Disaster Response Force, civil defence, revenue and other emergency response teams, according to the advisory.
People have been cautioned against venturing near rivers, nallahs, bridges or flood channels.
Vehicle owners have been advised to remove vehicles from low-lying areas and avoid unnecessary travel, officials said.
Any incidents of flooding, landslides, embankment breaches or stranded persons should be reported immediately to the District Emergency Operation Centre (DEOC), Rajouri, which is functioning round-the-clock.
The district administration said it is monitoring the situation and appealed to the public not to panic, avoid spreading rumours and rely only on official advisories.
Heavy rain was also reported in Ramban, Reasi and Poonch districts but there were no reports of any damage or imminent flood threats, officials said.
The weather office has forecast heavy rainfall and brief intense showers in few districts of Jammu division till Tuesday.
“Torrential rain and brief intense heavy showers may generate flash floods and landslides at vulnerable places during the next five days,” a meteorological department spokesperson said. (PTI)
